## Purpose and entry points
MLX is a C++ tensor/array runtime for ML research, exposing NumPy-like Python APIs plus C++ and C interfaces. It builds lazy, dynamic computation graphs with autodiff, vectorization, compilation, CPU/GPU execution, and unified-memory-oriented device handling. Public C++ surface starts at `mlx/mlx.h`, arrays at `mlx/array.h`, and Python native module bindings at `python/src/mlx.cpp`.

## Array graph and lazy execution
`array` represents tensor values and deferred primitive nodes; public operations construct graph nodes rather than necessarily materializing results. Evaluation, dependency scheduling, streams, events, fences, and device selection form the execution boundary.
- `mlx/array.cpp`
- `mlx/primitives.h`
- `mlx/scheduler.cpp`

## Operations, transforms, and compilation
The core operation layer covers elementwise, linalg, FFT, random, einsum, and specialized fast ML operations. Function transforms implement autodiff/custom VJPs and vectorization; compilation provides graph optimization/execution specialization while preserving dynamic graph semantics.
- `mlx/ops.cpp`
- `mlx/transforms.cpp`
- `mlx/compile.cpp`

## Backend abstraction and execution
Shared backend code defines reusable operation semantics and compiled-kernel interfaces, while device-specific backends own allocation, evaluation, synchronization, and kernel dispatch. CPU is always represented; Apple Metal and CUDA are alternative accelerators, with no-op backend variants supporting reduced builds.
- `mlx/backend/common/compiled.cpp`
- `mlx/backend/cpu/eval.cpp`
- `mlx/backend/metal/eval.cpp`
- `mlx/backend/cuda/eval.cpp`

## Accelerator kernels and external runtimes
Metal uses host C++ dispatch plus `.metal` kernels, including tuned Steel GEMM, convolution, and attention paths. CUDA uses `.cu` kernels and integrates CUDA libraries such as cuBLAS, cuDNN, and cuSOLVER. CPU includes Accelerate/CBLAS-style and SIMD GEMM implementations. CMake selects platform/backend dependencies.
- `mlx/backend/metal/metal.cpp`
- `mlx/backend/metal/kernels/steel/gemm/kernels/steel_gemm_fused.metal`
- `mlx/backend/cuda/cublas_utils.cpp`
- `mlx/CMakeLists.txt`

## Python framework layer
Pybind-style C++ bindings translate Python arrays, indexing, devices, transforms, and operation calls into the native runtime. Pure Python packages add neural-network modules, initialization, losses, optimizers, schedulers, utility tree operations, extension support, and distributed-launch utilities.
- `python/src/array.cpp`
- `python/src/ops.cpp`
- `python/mlx/nn/layers/base.py`
- `python/mlx/optimizers/optimizers.py`

## Distributed and persistence boundaries
Distributed primitives route collectives through selectable JACCL, MPI, NCCL, or ring implementations, with backend-specific device integration. Array persistence/import paths support safetensors and GGUF formats. These are optional build/runtime integrations rather than prerequisites for single-device computation.
- `mlx/distributed/distributed.cpp`
- `mlx/distributed/nccl/nccl.cpp`
- `mlx/io/safetensors.cpp`
- `mlx/io/gguf.cpp`

## Build and delivery
CMake drives the native library, selected CPU/Metal/CUDA/distributed components, examples, and tests. Python packaging (`setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`) builds/distributes wheels; GitHub workflows build and test Linux, macOS, Windows, wheels, releases, and documentation.
- `CMakeLists.txt`
- `setup.py`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `.github/workflows/build_and_test.yml`
